steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease one 12 cup muffin pan.
In a large bowl, combine egg, banana, brown sugar, applesauce and vanilla. In a separate bowl, sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
Gently stir flour mixture and oatmeal into banana mixture. Fold in chocolate chips and walnuts. Pour batter into prepared muffin cups.
Bake in preheated oven or 15 to 20 minutes, or until light brown. Remove muffins from pan and place on a wire rack to let cool before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Seminary Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Bananas and applesauce make these muffins very moist and tender.

review.reviewBody: I eliminated the chocolate chips and nuts and used whole wheat flour. They came out healthy and delicious!

Delicious! I skipped the chocolate chips and added more walnuts. I also used white whole wheat flour (King Arthur). I made mini muffins, bake time15 mins in my oven which runs a few degrees low. Perfect bite sized breakfast on the go, thanks for the recipe!

These muffins are delicious and easy! I reduced the brown sugar to 1/2 cup, used 3 small sized bananas, added a mix of dried fruits and coconut, and increased the walnuts to 3/4 cup. I think you could play with adding fruits or other nuts and not go wrong. The sweetness was enough, but not overpowering. Next time I will reduce the oats to 1/2 or 3/4 cup, as other reviewers did, and pulse the oats in the food processor first because the texture is a little rough.

I made these into 6 jumbo muffins, and they were ready in about 18 min. I also halved the oatmeal, as mentioned by a reviewer. I got by fine with that, and the texture was still dense. That was a good call; I don't think I'd like it with the full amount. I also used pecans and put aside a few tblsps that I topped the muffins with, along with some turbinado sugar. This would work well with raisins in place of the choc chips, too. Nice recipe.

I only made a few changes. I didn't have any applesauce so I used apple butter, I used 4 bananas because I had 4 turning black (3 would have been enough),I was low on brown sugar so I used 1/4c. brown sugar and 1/2c. white sugar, and lastly I used 1/2c. white flour and 1/2c. whole wheat flour. I wouldn't exactly call these "healthy" but they sure are yummy :) I probably could have used less sugar, especially since I used apple butter...next time I will only use 1/2c. of sugar. I made a mix of oatmeal, shredded coconut, and chopped walnuts, and sprinkled it (sparingly) over the tops of the muffins before I baked them. Really nice recipe, I'll make this one again! Yielded 16 regular sized muffins for me.

These are great. I followed the recipe as is then added 1/2 cup of chopped dates as well and topped with a sprinkle of oats and brown sugar. The texture is lovely, light and moist. I was afraid they'd be too sweet for my taste (I made them for my husband though and he likes more sweetness)but I really liked them. You could sub in any fruit etc. and use up those over-ripe bananas, which I keep in the freezer until I'm ready to use them.

I didn't have enough Banana....only 1/2 cup, so I doubled the applesauce and adder 1/4 cup of orange juice. I dint have any oats, so I added 3 packages of apple cinnamon instant oatmeal. I didn't have chocolate chips, so I left them out! The muffins were fabulous!!! So it's safe to say, if I stuck with the regular recipe they would have been fabulous too! Also, I baked them for 21 minutes!

So flavorful! I followed some of the comments-- reduced the sugar to half a cup (actually used coconut sugar), Doubled the applesauce, pulverized oats in food processor, and let oats sit in banana mixture for a few minutes. I also omitted the chocolate chips and didn't replace with anything. Didn't have walnuts so I used pecans. Yummo!! Will definitely make again, maybe will add some craisins. But these were definitely sweet enough without the extra sugar and chocolate chips.

Holy moly these are so GOOD! My son LOVED them(ate it in less than 2 minutes lol) as do my husband and I. This is the third muffin recipe I’ve tried in the past month and I will for sure be using this one every time for now on. I let the banana/applesauce mixture soak in the oats for 5 minutes before combing the flour mixture & added dried cranberries to half of them and they came out perfect. 5 stars for being kid friendly and for also being super yummy :)

This recipe was very forgiving, as I had to make several changes because my husband and I have both had gastric surgery. I try to cut back on the sugars and wheat flours and add extra proteins. In this recipe I used 6 tbs Splenda brown sugar substitute (1/2 recipe amount); 1/4 c white flour, 1/4 c coconut flour, and 1/2 c almond flour (to equal the 1 c flour the recipe calls for). I cut the salt to 1/2 tsp. and used regular oatmeal. I did not have quite enough bananas so I added a little bit of banana flavoring and used light sour cream to make up the difference in volume. For my add-ins I used 1 cup each of unsweetened coconut, pecans, and pepitas. (I did not use chocolate chips.) My large muffins took 28 min. to bake and tasted absolutely fabulous! I will certainly want to make these muffins again!

Loved these! Based on other reviews, I cut the brown sugar down to 1/2 cup (plenty sweet); used white whole wheat flour; subbed 1/4 cup of flax meal for some of the oatmeal; subbed fresh blueberries for the choc chips and left out the nuts because I didn't have any. Plugged it into my Weight Watchers smart points recipe creator and came out to 2 points per muffin! Outstanding!
I like these, but it's a lot of fiber. I'd probably adjust some ingredients for people who need lower fiber, but they were delicious!
I’ve been making these for years. I usually double the recipe.
I did not use walnuts. And I wish I would’ve ground the oats. They turned out great!
Good, easy, but not my absolute favorite.

I made this as written and it was perfect! The next weekend when the kids requested them again, I didn’t have any bananas so I used canned pumpkin in place of the banana and we had wonderfully wholesome pumpkin muffins!

Excellent recipe! Only change I made was leaving out the walnuts so that they could go to school. We will make these again! No other changes to recipe required. It also made the 12 full sized muffins as described which doesn't always happen.

I doubled the recipe and it only made 16 muffins after doubling.. I also used raisins in place of the chocolate chips and we all agree it’s more hearty and sweet that way! Eating these before cross country practice
these have potential but I don't love them. I used raisins instead of chocolate chips. they were a tad salty.
i love these muffins. so much flavor!
